content:
Unit 4 - Tone & Attitude — Title & Goal
Learn to master unit 4 - tone & attitude questions for the Digital SAT through a short concept, a modeled item, and targeted practice.

Key skill

Read the note and focus on what the question is really asking inside the passage.

  • Locate explicit claims and implicit ideas.
  • Ask: What is the passage mainly doing?
  • Match answers to the most general accurate statement.

Model item

Study how the evidence in the passage supports the correct answer.

Passage — The reviewer concedes the film’s technical skill but calls its plot ‘mechanical’ and its performances ‘dutiful.’

Question 1. The reviewer’s tone is best described as

  • reverent
  • dismissive
  • balanced but critical
  • celebratory
Mixed acknowledgment with negative descriptors → balanced but critical (C).

Quick practice

Try these quickly. Eliminate two choices before choosing your answer.

Sentence — The inventor’s ‘modest’ claim that the device ‘might help a few’ belies the team’s extensive marketing campaign.

Question 2. The tone of the sentence is most nearly

  • cautiously optimistic
  • skeptical
  • apologetic
  • resentful
‘Belies’ signals skepticism about the modesty → B.

Passage — Though the policy is framed as ‘streamlining,’ the memo lists several new forms to complete.

Question 3. The author’s attitude toward the policy is primarily

  • supportive
  • sarcastic
  • neutral
  • resigned
Contrast between ‘streamlining’ and new forms suggests sarcasm → B.

Next skill

Build on the previous skill. Compare how this question type reads the passage differently.

Note: Locate the exact phrase or sentence that proves your choice.

Another model item

Notice how small wording differences change the best answer.

Passage — The scientist calls the result ‘a promising first step’ and urges ‘caution until replicated by independent teams.’

Question 4. The tone is best characterized as

  • unqualified enthusiasm
  • measured and responsible
  • dismissive of others’ work
  • defensive
Optimism tempered by caution → B.

More practice

Aim for accuracy first, then speed. Re-check the evidence that rules out each wrong choice.

Sentence — ‘Of course the “upgrade” improved everything,’ she said, staring at the frozen screen.

Question 5. The tone is primarily

  • sincere
  • ironic
  • formal
  • indifferent

Mixed practice set

These mix multiple skills. Mark the question type before you start, then solve.

Passage — The author praises the volunteers as ‘indispensable’ and calls their work ‘the backbone of our effort.’

Question 6. The attitude toward the volunteers is most nearly

  • grudging
  • admiring
  • skeptical
  • playful
